    What's next for Red Sox after Jake Bauers deal? Plus more intel from the MLB GM Meetings

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (885 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings.
    • 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place?
    • For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this.

    With Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy?

    For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.

    Tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a major-league game in 2026, is right now on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors.

    Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy.

    Sources indicate that boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question.

    It has been revealed that "I'm not going to speak to that right now," he mentioned "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of.".

    Sources indicate that now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.

    Sources indicate that because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract.

    Sources indicate that hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club.

    According to recent reports, none of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.

    The risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels.

    "He's got a world of potential," said Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright major-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field.".

    Sources indicate that the Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time.

    It has been revealed that bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway.

    In a recent development, with Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.

    One is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.

    Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade.

    Naturally, there is some apprehension.

    It has been revealed that "I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow remarked. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately.".

    Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

    📅 09 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3150 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.
    • The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.
    • It has been revealed that that goal also was supposed to set up penalties.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

    The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

    It has been revealed that that goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

    Industry observers note that that confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

    Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE.

    Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

    And considering Johor are one game away from setting a newly introduced world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

    After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

    The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

    In a recent development, while they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

    For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

    It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

    Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

    Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

    Industry observers note that considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

    Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

    Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

    There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

    Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

    The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

    Recent findings suggest that that was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

    There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

    Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

    Industry observers note that mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

    It’s been an entertaining match.

    It has been revealed that it’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

    It has been revealed that as if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

    In a recent development, chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

    A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    Sources indicate that just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

    “The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

    “We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

    In a recent development, “We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”.

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    It has been revealed that loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Recent findings suggest that steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    In a recent development, finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an problem is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Houston Rockets improved to 11-3 on the season with a 147-119 beatdown of the Washington Wizards on Sunday night.

    According to recent reports, while Houston is no stranger to an offensive explosion, ranking second in the NBA this season in offensive rating (121.2), the 147 points scored on Sunday were 12 more than they've scored in a game this season. It was a balanced scoring effort as a team, as six players reached double figures and three scored at least 25 points -- including Tari Eason off the bench.

    That 25-point performance represents a new season high for Eason -- his previous best was a 19-point effort against the Hawks -- as he went 10 for 14 from the field and 3 of 5 from 3-point range in 30 minutes off the bench. That effort earned Eason the honor of the walk-off TV interview, during which he gave a brutally honest (and hilarious) answer for why he was able to set a new season high and do so efficiently.

    "Shit, the Wizards, for real. It was them," Eason said.

    Tari Eason on what allowed him to have a season-high 25 points off the bench tonight:"Shit, the Wizards, for real." pic.twitter.com/t4bOwtzw5r.

    Recent findings suggest that A+ work here, no notes. Eason could've puffed out his chest after beating up on the Wizards or complimented his teammates for allowing him to get in a rhythm, but instead chose the honest route rarely taken by players in a post-game interview and simply admitted that anyone could get buckets on Washington.

    Recent findings suggest that the Wizards are not the worst defense in the NBA -- that honor belongs to the Chicago Bulls -- but they are 25th in defensive rating and certainly do not boast very many elite defenders. Clearly, Eason didn't feel like he was doing anything special or out of the ordinary on Sunday night on his way to 25 points off the bench, and gave credit where it was due to the other team.

    Unfortunately for the Wizards, it is not credit they'd like to take, and this feels like the kind of (earned) disrespect that should light some kind of fire under Washington.

    #96296. How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1398 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1398 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light.
    • Let's take a look at four major reasons.
    • According to recent reports, giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light. It initially came against weaker opponents, with wins over the Pacers, Clippers, Jazz and Kings getting them back near .500. But these back-to-back wins over Cleveland (on Friday) and Detroit (on Saturday) put a real stamp on this stretch. After all the panic, Miami has won seven of nine and is tied for the East's No. 4 seed entering this week.

    How have they turned things around? Let's take a look at four major reasons.

    According to recent reports, giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins. The concerns over their offensive fit -- as relative non-shooters who operate largely in the same spots -- have quieted, but also a good bit of this production is coming independent of one another as Erik Spoelstra is staggering their minutes between the start of each half and fourth-quarter closing time.

    With shooters all around, Adebayo and Antetokounmpo are free to attack maximum interior space and exploit soft midrange spots, which has been the bread and butter of this run.

    Every mid range jumper from Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo against Cleveland last night: pic.twitter.com/jeamVaSLhk.

    It has been revealed that as pointed out by Couper Moorhead of NBA.com, the Heat face more drop-coverage defense (when the major who's guarding the ball screener falls back toward the rim rather than stepping up to the level of the screen or even higher to contest the shooter coming off the screen) than any other offense in the league. That's because nobody fears Miami's pull-up 3-point shooters, and because Giannis and Bam are such forceful attackers of the rim.

    The soft spot is in between, outside the restricted circle but inside the 3-point line, or even better inside the free-throw line. It's the dreaded midrange zone, where defenses are happy to, concede shots to players like Giannis and Bam, and right now they are both knocking these supposedly inefficient looks down at ridiculous rates.

    These are by far career-high percentages for both guys, and they are coming on career-high frequencies from these zones (over 30% of their total shot attempts in the 3-10 range). Over these last nine games, Giannis is a scorching 22 for 33 from 10-19 feet while Adebayo -- who has also been the best post scorer in the league at 1.26 PPP on 4.8 post-ups per game -- is 30 for 44 from 5-14 feet.

    Recent findings suggest that they are absolutely wearing these outer-paint shots out, and if defenses keep with the drop coverage, these shots are likely to remain consistently available. It's not to say they'll keep making them at this rate, of course. But to have established these go-zones is a significant step for Miami's half-court offense, because we all know how dangerous they are in the open floor as the highest-frequency and second-highest-scoring transition team.

    Now add in the fact that Miami kills teams on the glass with Giannis and Bam on the court (over these last nine, they are grabbing 78.7 percent of all available defensive rebounds and 37.8% of all offensive rebounds, both of which would lead the league), and in the turnover battle, and what you have is a Heat team that is getting a lot more true shot attempts than its opponents (almost 10 more per 100 possessions).

    According to recent reports, that is everything in today's possession-obsessed NBA. Get up more shots than your opponent by generating second-chance opportunities on the offensive boards and by creating more turnovers than you cough up, and you're in a good spot. Make those extra shots at the rate Miami is right now, and you're almost unbeatable.

    Industry observers note that mitchell has gone from a guy perhaps playing to stay in the league, or at least in an NBA rotation, to a current top-three Most Improved Player candidate at FanDuel (+900). He's blowing his previous production away.

    In a recent development, the Heat are a low-volume pick-and-roll team for the same reasons they're a prime candidate for drop coverage: They don't have those kinds of pull-up shooters. Mitchell can punish drops with pull-up 3s on occasion (8 for 20 so far, per Synergy), but more importantly he's the one most often hitting Bam and Giannis in those soft-pocket midrange spots we talked about -- in addition to the rim rolls, cuts and kick-out 3s that open up as he breaches the paint, often in transition.

    Sources indicate that of Mitchell's 119 assists so far, 55 have gone to Giannis and Bam, and he has directly set up a 3-point make 37 times. Those 9.2 assists per game lead the league among qualified players, and the 257 points his assists have generated rank second only to Trae Young's 260, per PBP Stats. Young is making $49 million this year. Mitchell is making $12 million.

    According to recent reports, then there is the shooting. Mitchell has steadily improved from range throughout his career, but this season he's on fire at 43% on catch-and-shoot 3s, per Synergy, as part of Miami's spacing around Bam and Giannis. We saw all of Mitchell's tools in his 22-point/17-assist masterpiece against Cleveland.

    Davion Mitchell ABSURD statline vs Cavs: 22 PTS | 5 REB | 17 AST | 7/14 FG | 66 TS% pic.twitter.com/b0d8I1XHDy.

    Thompson isn't the player he was in his prime. His defense has especially declined, and he's not going to be putting up any more 37-point quarters. But he's still a sniper.

    Thompson is splashing 42% on almost 10 3s a game, and his 48 total 3-pointers rank third league-wide, and his 15.3 PPG are the most he's averaged since leaving Golden State. He's been especially hot of late, averaging 20 PPG on 48/45 shooting splits over his last seven games.

    Klay Thompson was amazing vs the Pistons26 PTS - 4 AST - 6 3PM - 10/17 FGM Found a latest home pic.twitter.com/JvQju9Hais.

    Over the last seven games, Miami is plus-11.7 with Thompson on the court and minus-3.7 when he's off. That's the best split on the team. The starting lineup of Mitchell, Bam, Giannis, Thompson and Pelle Larsson (who has been massive in this turnaround, too, since his promotion to the first five), the Heat are outscoring opponents by 23 points per 100 possessions, and Thompson has been particularly effective playing alongside Giannis. With those two on the court as Bam rests, Miami is drumming teams by 31.6 points per 100, per Databallr.

    Miami's defense was expected to be a strength, and when people looked up and saw a bottom-barrel rating, it was jarring. Some of that, if not most of it, could be attributed to inordinately hot shooting by their opponents, which wasn't likely to continue. And indeed it hasn't.

    Through the first seven games, Miami opponents were shooting 41.8% from 3 and 50% from the midrange, per Cleaning the Glass. That made for a 58.7 effective field-goal percentage, despite Miami's defense registering a top-three expected eFG% (52.9) based on the shots they were surrendering, per Cleaning the Glass.

    Translation: the Heat were, and are, forcing generally inefficient shots, but to start the year those shots were going in at a rate of almost 6% better than expected. That was the worst, or unluckiest, mark in the league, however you want to look at it.

    Recent findings suggest that cut to this four-game win streak, over which opponents are down to 35.2% from 3 with a 53.9 eFG% against an expected 54%, per CTG. That's in part because Miami has cut the number of wide-open 3s (nearest defender at least six feet away) it was allowing to start the year almost in half (to start, they were surrendering 16 wide-open 3s every night, but over this four-game winning streak they are down to 9.1, stingiest in the league). Even better, their opponents have come down from a 45.5% conversion rate on those wide-open 3s to 40%.

    All of which is to say, Miami's opponent shooting is coming back to earth. Hot shooting can render any defense helpless, but over time, if you're forcing a team into tough shots from tough spots, the averages are going to swing back your way eventually. Miami is starting to see that happen.

    Texans vs. Colts prediction: Houston looks to bounce back on 'TNF' vs. lowly Indy after rough Week 10 loss

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts.
    • Recent findings suggest that houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes.
    • The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts.

    Recent findings suggest that houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot.

    The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline.

    Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.

    The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces.

    In a recent development, instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing.

    Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL. Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions.

    Industry observers note that the Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games.

    According to recent reports, the Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan, including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up.

    Sources indicate that taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state.

    C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season.

    The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner, either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins.

    Industry observers note that it's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence.

    This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense.

Until then, we can hope to see some player movement, such as the Red Sox signing Jake Bauers.

    In the meantime, let's round up the news and rumors for the day.

    It has been revealed that the Padres are in desperate need of starting pitching, should they wish to continue contending. The rotation right now would be Joe Musgrove, Randy Vásquez, JP Sears, Jhony Brito and a shrugging emoji. Sure enough, they are all over the rumor mill for rotation help.

    Industry observers note that the San Diego Union-Tribune reports that they've shown interest in "virtually every starting pitcher" in free agency, "from Tarik Skubal on down. Further, ESPN reports that the Padres have a meeting set up with Skubal but have also shown interest in Freddy Peralta, as well as Michael King, Nick Pivetta and Nick Martinez.

    Expect them to remain active until they land at least two starters.

    Sources indicate that it's no secret that the Diamondbacks are open to trading All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. The Blue Jays have been sniffing around, and now the Orioles have emerged as a suitor, per MLB.com.

    Industry observers note that this one is interesting in that it's not a natural fit. The Orioles have extra infielders and have been said to be shopping infielders in order to land outfield help. Between second and third base, the Orioles have Jackson Holliday, Jordan Westburg, Blaze Alexander, Coby Mayo and Christian Encarnacion-Strand. Presumably, if they are able to swing a deal for Marte, there would be some shuffling with more trades and/or moving someone to the outfield.

    The Mets could have an opening at first base as things currently stand and they've checked in on free agent Ty France, according to the New York Post.

    At the moment, the Mets are looking at Jared Young (coming off a scary head injury), Mark Vientos and Jorge Polanco as options at first base.

    France, 32 and probably considered a journeyman at this point, had a big season in 2026 for the Padres. He hit .295/.363/.502 (139 OPS+) with 21 homers, 72 RBI and a career-high 4.5 WAR.

    Recent findings suggest that reliever Jonathan Loáisiga is close to signing with a new team, reports ESPN. The Dodgers are among five teams involved, with the New York Post adding the Phillies, Mets, Yankees and Blue Jays to the mix.

    In 67 outings last season for Arizona, Loáisiga pitched to a 2.42 ERA, 1.03 WHIP and had 48 strikeouts in 67 innings.

    Sources indicate that the Yankees have re-signed left-handed reliever Tim Hill to a one-year, $2.25 million deal with a $2.5 million club option for 2028, per ESPN. Hill, 36, made 67 appearances last season with a 4.60 ERA, 1.14 WHIP and 25 strikeouts in 58 ⅔ innings. He held lefties to a .213/.265/.346 line.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot at the moment “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

    In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

    It has been revealed that “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

    Industry observers note that “We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

    Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

    Industry observers note that alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

    A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

    Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

    Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

    In a recent development, cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

    Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

    Sources indicate that this afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under fresh management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

    Industry observers note that in pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

    Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

    Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

    #96286. 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1638 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1638 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, this Friday, Nov.
    • Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary.
    • With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, this Friday, Nov. 20, is an notable date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.

    Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and substantial names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.

    With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.

    Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.

    Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028).

    Recent findings suggest that former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That said, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.

    Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029).

    The American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with New York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.

    Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028).

    It has been revealed that A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.

    Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.

    Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028).

    In 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a major chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.

    Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028).

    Recent findings suggest that right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young stated his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.

    Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027).

    Doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.

    Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027).

    A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get substantial offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.

    Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029).

    Recent findings suggest that two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year.     Recent findings suggest that 2. Emmett Johnson (vs. ARI) - 119.5 proj. total yards.

    It has been revealed that the Chiefs seem to be planning for Kenneth Walker III (groin) to rest another week after Johnson more than held his own in last week's blowout win. The rookie, who reminds me of a Bucky Irving type on film, handled 22 carries and six receptions, leading to 32.1 half PPR points on 20.6 expected points. Those are obviously elite RB1 numbers. Kansas City simply doesn't have another RB it trusts for the moment, and the offense is firing on all cylinders against mediocre opponents.

    Recent findings suggest that the Cardinals are just that. They've allowed the fifth-most rush YPG (130) and were just schooled by Blake Corum (119 total yards) last week. A huge 28.0-point team total as 15.5-point favorites (!!!!!!) awaits.

The Panthers have a 23.0-point team total (12th) as near-field-goal favorites.

    4. Javonte Williams (vs. TEN) - 92.5 proj. total yards.

    Let's keep this simple: Williams is an upside RB1 whenever the Cowboys have a 31.5-point team total, as they do here.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    It has been revealed that the Titans have allowed nearly 1,500 yards over their last three games, the most in a 3-game stretch in their franchise history. Trading away mega-star DT Jeffery Simmons and Pro Bowl-caliber S Amani Hooker won't help. The starting RB against Tennessee has cleared 100 total yards in four straight contests.

    5. James Cook III (vs. MIA) - 110.5 proj. total yards.

    Sources indicate that cook ranks as the RB6 in half PPR points per game on RB8 usage across his last four contests, averaging 23 carries (second) and 109.8 rushing yards per game.     According to recent reports, the Bills are expected to beat the Dolphins by 16.5 points with a bonkers 31-point team total. Miami just lost DTs Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers to injured reserve. I don't have to tell you this is a great spot.

    6. Christian McCaffrey (vs. MIN) - 87.5 proj. total yards.

    Sources indicate that when McCaffrey is in the United States of America this year, he averages 22.7 half PPR points (RB2) on 16.3 expected half PPR points (RB6). Turns out, Kaelon Black is a fine role player but nothing more than that to CMC. Remember to go outside in early September while the weather is nice.

    According to recent reports, anyways, this will be a great test for the 49ers as they face the Vikings in Mexico City.     7. Jonah Coleman (vs. LV) - 97.5 proj. total yards.

    With R.J. Harvey (knee) on IR, the backfield has been down to just two. Coleman leapfrogged J.K. Dobbins over the last pair of games, finishing as the RB7 and RB9 in expected half PPR points. Dobbins won't play on passing downs, so Coleman is grabbing some receptions alongside his rushing role. He has been just fine on tape in a good situation.

    Speaking of, the Raiders are generous when it comes to fantasy points for RBs. They've allowed, oh, just 176 rushing yards per game this month. Both Seahawks RBs played well behind three backup linemen, and CMC (RB4), Braelon Allen (RB7) and Kyren Williams (RB12) were fantasy RBs this month. Denver is listed as 10-point home favorites with an implied team total of 25.25 points (eighth).

    #96280. 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction

    2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1152 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.
    • The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman.
    • As a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.

    The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.

    As a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut.

    The results will be declared on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.

    Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason.

    As alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote.

    It has been revealed that players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers.

    Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980.".

    We'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote.

    Giants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in.

    As for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in.

    Then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote.

    This is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point.

    He did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a latest high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.

    While some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit.

    Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains:.

    In a recent development, he only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028.

    Some of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing:.

    The bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far.

    In a recent development, K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point.

    In a recent development, if K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen?

    Who else is back on the ballot? A quick look:.

    Posey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though.

    I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).

    On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that this season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

    In a recent development, that's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He currently has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

    It has been revealed that during the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

    Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

    With the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

    With Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

    It has been revealed that boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

    In a recent development, acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

    The Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are presently riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

    In a recent development, dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots. The way the Wizards are using him is confusing at times. Dybantsa is in somewhat of a weird situation because of the Wizards' roster. Washington handed Trae Young a huge contract this offseason that is already aging poorly. Dybantsa should be the focus of the offense. He should be touching the ball and shooting it even more than he is already. I have been impressed with Dybantsa's defense this season.

    Bills to retire franchise legend Andre Reed's No. 83 during the 2027 season

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (460 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Buffalo Bills will honor another key member of their iconic 1990s team.
    • Reed, who starred in Buffalo from 1985-99, is the franchise's all-time career leader with 941 catches, 13,095 yards and 86 touchdowns.
    • Reed has joined former teammates Jim Kelly, Bruce Smith and Thurman Thomas as the fourth Bills player in the organization's history to have his jersey number retired.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Buffalo Bills will honor another key member of their iconic 1990s team. The franchise revealed on Thursday night that it will retire Hall of Fame receiver Andre Reed's No. 83 during the 2027 season.

    Reed, who starred in Buffalo from 1985-99, is the franchise's all-time career leader with 941 catches, 13,095 yards and 86 touchdowns. He had an additional 85 catches for 1,229 yards and nine touchdowns in 17 playoff games.

    Reed has joined former teammates Jim Kelly, Bruce Smith and Thurman Thomas as the fourth Bills player in the organization's history to have his jersey number retired.

    Kelly, Thomas and Bills owner Terry Pegula surprised Reed with the news.

    It has been revealed that “There’s no family like your football family.” Some special guests revealed up to One Bills Drive to surprise @Andre_Reed83 with the news. @JimKelly1212 | @thurmanthomas pic.twitter.com/LUDGDB0h8c.

    "Oh man, it's almost like the moment when we all got the call for him going into the Hall of Fame," Thomas stated. "We knew that he deserved to be in the Hall of Fame, and it was kind of the same thing. One of the four guys that, when you mention the Bills, his name is always mentioned.

    "You saw his work ethic when we were in training camp together for 12 years, like, yeah, that guy is special, and he was a big part of our run to try to win a Super Bowl here. There aren't too many people today that go over the middle as much as Andre Reed did back in the day. He took a lot of punishment, but he was always there for us.".

    It has been revealed that reed was an integral part of Buffalo's historic run of success during the 1990s. While they didn't win a Super Bowl, Buffalo made history by becoming the first (and last) team to play in four consecutive Super Bowls. Reed caught eight passes for 153 yards in Buffalo's third of four consecutive trips to the major game.

    About time. Andre Reed’s number should have already been retiredGlad the Bills are finally giving him his due. Best WR in team history pic.twitter.com/FWDroOn6a7 https://t.co/lVC62BJ2hU.

    Buffalo's run also included the largest come-from-behind win in playoff history. The Bills overcame a 35-3 deficit to defeat the Oilers in the 1992 wild card round. Reed caught three consecutive touchdowns during Buffalo's comeback.

    According to recent reports, january 3, 1993° 1992 AFC WILD CARD °LARGEST COMEBACK IN #NFL POSTSEASON HISTORYThe Oilers take a 35-3 lead over the #Bills early in the third quarter.Buffalo claws all the way back to lead 38-35, but Houston ties it to force overtime.#BillsMafia prevails in OT, 41-38. pic.twitter.com/SrZn6jGsZf.

    Reed was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • Sources indicate that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Upcoming Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams declared the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Sources indicate that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He remarked at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    In a recent development, after trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Upcoming Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Goaltending has been an issue in Fresh Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    According to recent reports, in the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    In a recent development, in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    It has been revealed that the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Latest Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    It has been revealed that let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    In a recent development, that noted, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    Recent findings suggest that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    According to recent reports, daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his fresh team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    Recent findings suggest that if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    According to recent reports, the Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.
